svg.title: MAINLINE architecture: how a judge's request reaches a refusal
svg.desc: A judge's browser or curl, holding no credential, calls a public AWS Lambda Function URL in ap-southeast-1. The Lambda runs the demo API and reads its database connection string from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. It speaks to CockroachDB Cloud Basic over pgwire, where three steps make the refusal: a trigger projects the count of unanswered obligations onto the row being written, a composite foreign key pins a finished merge to its epoch, and a named CHECK constraint refuses. Amazon CloudWatch holds the function's log group and alarms and separately reads the AWS/Bedrock counters. Drawn outside the request path, in a dashed panel: MAINLINE's recall agent with Amazon Bedrock in ap-southeast-2, the CockroachDB Cloud Managed MCP Server, and CockroachDB Agent Skills which is designed and not exercised.
svg.text: MAINLINE — how a judge's request reaches a refusal
Everything above the dashed panel is on the live request path a judge can call today. The dashed panel is real in this repository and is not called while a judge is looking.
Service and product names are plain text; no logo or trademark appears in this image. Every label's source is listed in docs/submission/DIAGRAMS.md.
THE DEMO'S REQUEST PATH
— no agent and no model runs here; the four beats a judge presses are SQL. MAINLINE's agent is in the dashed panel at the foot.
A judge's browser, or curl
No account. No login. No credential of ours. Nothing to install.
HTTPS, anonymous
GET /v1/health · POST /v1/demo/gate-run
AWS Lambda Function URL — ap-southeast-1 (Singapore)
authorization_type = NONE — open on purpose. An IAM-signed URL with nothing
authorised to sign for it would be a demo nobody, including a judge, could reach.
AWS Lambda — the demo API
Python 3.13 on arm64 · 256 MB · 14-second timeout · ap-southeast-1 (Singapore)
It carries no AWS SDK. The one AWS call it makes — to Parameter Store, right —
is signed by hand, so the package behaves the same on a laptop and in Lambda.
logs
Amazon CloudWatch
The function's log group and its four metric alarms exist in the account.
No record in this repository shows any alarm ever firing, so what is
evidenced here is the alarm, never the threshold.
Separately, and off the request path: read-only calls read the
AWS/Bedrock counters — invocations and token counts — that witness the
model runs in the dashed panel below. Those counters are the one witness
in this project that AWS wrote and we did not.
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
Holds the database connection string, encrypted. The function reads it
once when it starts cold, then keeps it in memory. It is never an
environment variable, so it is not in the configuration anyone can list.
pgwire over TLS · same region
CockroachDB Cloud — Basic tier
cluster mainline-dev · database mainline_demo · CockroachDB CCL v26.2.5 · aws-ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) · migration chain 271 of 271 applied
1 · PROJECT
Two triggers — rules the database runs itself
on every write. One fills in an obligation's
severity from the record of what caused the
rule, overwriting whatever the writer gave it.
The other adds one to a plain count on the
permit row. Neither takes the writer's word.
check_project · check_materialised
2 · PIN
The same trigger ticks an epoch — a counter
that rises whenever a new obligation appears.
A finished merge takes a composite foreign key
onto the permit and the epoch it finished
under, so a new obligation cannot be attached
to a merge already done. Not refused: it
cannot be expressed.
epoch_pin_permit (permit_id, gate_epoch)
3 · REFUSE
A named CHECK constraint rejects the write: a
permit may not reach merged while that count is
above zero. SQLSTATE 23514 is the five-character
code a database returns for a violated CHECK.
Forge the count and the gate's own function
re-derives it and raises P0001 instead.
gate_closed_when_issued
mainline.fn_permit_merge_gate
Beat three forges the projected count to zero and tries the merge again. It is refused anyway, because the gate re-derives the count rather than trusting it.
All four beats run in one SERIALIZABLE transaction that ends in ROLLBACK — persisted: false. Use case 2, the change request, refuses the same way and has no admission beat.
OUTSIDE THE DEMO'S REQUEST PATH — REAL IN THIS REPOSITORY, NOT CALLED WHILE A JUDGE IS LOOKING
The four beats a judge presses are SQL against CockroachDB and call no model. Drawing Amazon Bedrock inside the path above would be an overclaim.
The recall agent · Amazon Bedrock
The program that reads the site's memory runs
here in the repository, not in the Lambda
above. It calls Amazon Bedrock — Claude to
reason, Titan Text Embeddings v2 for the
numbers that stand for a clause — in region
ap-southeast-2 (Sydney). It then searches
CockroachDB's vector index for nearby clauses.
CockroachDB Cloud Managed MCP Server
A second channel, separate from the path
above, and it has been exercised: 15 of 16
questions answered, with the run's own verdict
left at DIVERGED — KNOWN GAP. It needs our
CockroachDB Cloud key, which we cannot
publish — so it can never be the way a judge
gets in.
CockroachDB Agent Skills — DESIGNED
Written, on disk, each shipping a script a
reader can run. No run of either is recorded
under evidence/. It is drawn here as a note
rather than as a path, because nothing in
this repository has exercised it. A box with
an arrow into the picture would be a claim
we have not earned.
MAINLINE · CockroachDB x AWS, "Build with Agentic Memory" · the file and line behind every label on this diagram is listed in docs/submission/DIAGRAMS.md section 1.
